summary: Sporting News's Week 12 standard-league fantasy football running back rankings for Thanksgiving week, with no byes and games on four days. Sloan Piva ranks 63 backs and picks sleepers (Rhamondre Stevenson, Kyren Williams, Zach Charbonnet, AJ Dillon), busts (Derrick Henry, Chuba Hubbard, Miles Sanders, Khalil Herbert) and covers key injuries (Kenneth Walker III, Aaron Jones, De'Von Achane, D'Onta Foreman).
one_line: Sporting News ranks 63 running backs for Week 12 of the 2023 fantasy football season, with sleepers, busts and injury updates.
key_facts: Week 12 has no byes, with NFL games on four days: Thursday, Friday, Sunday and Monday.
Only three regular-season weeks remain before the fantasy playoffs, and trade deadlines have passed in most leagues.
Christian McCaffrey (49ers @ Seahawks) is ranked RB1, followed by Austin Ekeler (Chargers vs. Ravens) and Saquon Barkley (Giants vs. Patriots).
Saquon Barkley had 140 total yards and two TDs against the Commanders; the Patriots have allowed 116 scrimmage yards per game and nine total TDs to RBs.
David Montgomery and Jahmyr Gibbs of the Lions are ranked 4th and 5th against a Packers defense that had allowed nearly 140 all-purpose yards per game to RBs entering Week 11.
Tony Pollard averaged 5.1 yards per carry against Carolina and scored his first TD since Week 1; he is ranked 6th.
Kenneth Walker III suffered an oblique injury in Week 11, which Pete Carroll called "legit"; Zach Charbonnet is ranked 25th as the likely bell-cow.
Aaron Jones (knee) and Emanuel Wilson (shoulder) were hurt in Week 11, making AJ Dillon (ranked 27th) the expected lead back for the 4-6 Packers.
De'Von Achane appeared to aggravate his MCL injury after returning from IR against the Raiders; Salvon Ahmed went on IR with a foot injury, so Jeff Wilson Jr. is a handcuff stash.
Derrick Henry has just 64 total yards on 23 touches (2.8 yards per touch) over two weeks, but is still ranked 20th and recommended as a start against the Panthers.
Rhamondre Stevenson has 231 yards from scrimmage and a TD over New England's past two games and faces a Giants defense; Washington's run game gained 174 yards and a TD against the Giants.
No Carolina back has had a 60-yard rushing game since Oct. 15, so Chuba Hubbard and Miles Sanders are labeled players not to start.
Khalil Herbert gained 35 yards on 16 carries in his return against the Lions, while Justin Fields ran for 100 yards.
Dameon Pierce is ranked 43rd, with Devin Singletary described as the new RB1 for the Texans.
